eligibility.evidence: Sec 2.1, 2.3 (pp.245-247): LLMs given a psycholinguistic sentence-continuation task, items based on Cai et al. 2013, 2022; new LLM responses analysed (Sec 3.3). Meets E1-E6.

A.title: What to Predict? Exploring How Sentence Structure Influences Contrast Predictions in Humans and Large Language Models
A.venue: Workshop on Cognitive Modeling and Computational Linguistics (CMCL)

paradigms.name: Sentence continuation: contrast prediction after Mandarin double-object vs prepositional-object ditransitives
paradigms.source_paper: Cai et al. 2013; Cai et al. 2022 (items based on)

D.population: native Mandarin speakers (written n=50, original spoken n=50, normalised spoken n=48 after exclusions; 164 recruited), online via Qualtrics and Zoom
D.metric: mixed-model beta of the structure effect (recipient minus theme contrast share, PO vs DO); Pearson r of response-pattern profiles

effects.es_metric: mixed-model beta (structure x continuation type); human = written group
effects.label: EXAGGERATED
effects.location: Sec 3.3.2-3.3.3, p.249; human beta Sec 3.3.1 p.249; GPT-4o vs written human beta 0.61, p<.001; spoken humans beta 0.35 and 0.28 reported separately; Pearson r vs written 0.75, spoken 0.82 (Fig 2)

E.headline: Humans and LLMs both shift contrast predictions with sentence structure; all three LLMs show larger structural effects than humans, with GPT-4o closest to human data.

G.notes: No model versions, temperatures or query dates; no code/data link or item list. Single paradigm; 50 sessions per model approximates human n. Qwen written and normalised-spoken comparison betas are identical (0.90, t 8.83), possible typo. Human beta chosen: written group (first reported).
